class.name: SnowSurface3D
class.brief_description: Deep snow as geometry, with prints, tracks and rims that bodies sink into.
class.description: A mesh around the camera lifted to the ground plus the depth of the [SnowCover3D] pack, so snow has real volume: it casts shadows, buries small things and is traced as geometry under path tracing. Snow thinner than [member min_depth] stays a material effect. Nodes in [member deform_groups] press it. A pressed column compacts toward [member compacted_density] and pushes [member rim_share] of the snow it loses into a rim, so mass is kept. Loaded bodies sink by Bekker's pressure-sinkage relation (Bekker 1969). On a frozen crust ([member SnowCover3D.crust_enabled]) a body whose pressure is under what the crust bears ([method SnowCover3D.get_crust_strength_at]) stands on it, and only the snow over it compacts; a heavier one, or one driven through, breaks it: the crust cracks around the hole out to about its plate length (0.13 m for 2 cm, growing as thickness^(3/4)), the pieces tip in, and the rim heaps in plates. A heightfield collision patch follows the deformed surface, so bodies rest in their own tracks. New snow and wind fill prints; as the pack around them settles their depth shrinks; when the pack melts they go with it. Tiles of prints the field leaves are kept and come back.

method.name: bekker_sinkage
method.description: Returns Bekker's pressure-sinkage depth in metres, [code](p / (kc / b + kphi))^(1 / n)[/code], for a load of [param pressure_kpa] kilopascals on a patch [param width] metres wide (Bekker 1969).

method.name: clear_deformation
method.description: Removes every print and rim, in the live field and in the tile cache.

method.name: get_cached_tile_count
method.description: Returns the number of deformation tiles kept for areas the field has left.

method.name: get_deform_rect
method.description: Returns the world rectangle (x and z) of the live deformation field.

method.name: get_dent_at
method.description: Returns how far the snow is pressed below its undisturbed surface at [param position], in metres.

method.name: get_moved_volume
method.description: Returns the volume of the prints (x) and of the rims (y) over the live field, in cubic metres.

method.name: get_rim_at
method.description: Returns the height of pushed-up snow at [param position], in metres.

method.name: get_step_time_msec
method.description: Returns the CPU time of the last physics step (presses, refill, collision and upload), in milliseconds.

method.name: get_surface_height_at
method.description: Returns the height of the snow surface at [param position]: the ground plus the pack depth, minus prints, plus rims. Where the snow is thinner than [member min_depth] it returns the ground.

method.name: get_surface_material
method.description: Returns the surface's material, for its parameters.

method.name: press
method.description: Presses the snow down to [param bottom] (the world height of a body's underside) within [param radius] of [param position]: a bowl when [param round], flat otherwise. [param sink] presses that much further below the undisturbed surface (Bekker sinkage). Snow never goes below what [member compacted_density] allows; [member rim_share] of what moves goes into a rim around the print. A [param velocity] (m/s; bodies in the deform groups get theirs from their motion) leans the rim forward: a fast body shoves snow ahead of it in a bow wave that rides in front and spills to the sides, full at 4 m/s. Returns the volume moved, in cubic metres. Nothing happens unless the underside touches the snow.

method.name: press_box
method.description: Like [method press], with a flat rectangular print [param size] wide (x) and long (y), turned by [param yaw] radians about up: a boot, a runner, a crate.

method.name: refresh_ground
method.description: Samples the ground again, for example after the terrain was carved.

members.member: Bekker's cohesive modulus, kN/m^(n+1). The default is Wong's value for snow ([i]Theory of Ground Vehicles[/i]).
Bekker's frictional modulus, kN/m^(n+2).
Bekker's sinkage exponent.
The area one boot presses for a [CharacterBody3D] in a deform group, in square metres, unless the node has a [code]snow_contact_area[/code] meta.
The mass of a [CharacterBody3D] in a deform group, in kilograms, unless the node has a [code]snow_mass[/code] meta.
If [code]true[/code], a heightfield body follows the deformed snow surface around the camera, so bodies stand on the snow and sink into their own prints.
The width of the collision patch, in metres.
The physics layers of the collision patch.
The physics mask of the collision patch.
How many times a second the collision patch follows the snow.
The density pressed snow reaches under a boot or a wheel, in kg/m3. Snow already that dense takes no prints.
How close an underside must come to the snow, in metres, to press it.
If [code]true[/code], nodes in [member deform_groups] press prints and tracks into the snow.
The width of the deformation field around the camera, in metres. The mesh is at [member detail_spacing] over it.

Groups whose [Node3D]s press the snow. The shape is the first [CollisionShape3D] child: spheres and capsules press a bowl, upright cylinders and boxes a flat print (boxes turned with the shape, so a box per foot gives boot prints), lying cylinders a wheel track. [RigidBody3D]s sink by their mass, [CharacterBody3D]s by [member character_mass], any node by a [code]snow_mass[/code] meta; other nodes press only as deep as their underside. A [code]snow_radius[/code] meta overrides the radius. The grass trample group is included so one set of movers drives both.
Texels across the deformation field (a multiple of 64).
The mesh spacing over the deformation field, in metres. Fragments shade the finer texel detail.
The distance over which the snow tapers to the ground at the mesh edge, in metres; beyond it materials carry the snow.
The width of the snow mesh around the camera, in metres.
The node the mesh and the deformation field follow. Empty: the current camera.
The spacing of the ground samples under the mesh, in metres.
How many 4 m deformation tiles are kept for areas the field has left (16 KB each); the oldest go first.
The largest mesh spacing, at the outer edge.
The strength of the millimetre wind ripples in the shading.
Snow thinner than this, in metres, is left to the materials ([member BaseMaterial3D.snow_enabled]); the surface tucks under the ground there.
The share of each new snowfall that settles into prints, on top of the snow that covers everything evenly.
The share of pressed snow pushed into a rim around the print; the rest compacts in place.
The [SnowCover3D] giving the pack depth, albedo and wetness. Empty: the active one.
A tint on the snow albedo.
How fast wind fills prints and planes rims, per weather hour at full drift ([method SnowCover3D.get_drift_factor]).
